v2.note: Both figures are right: CL FY2023 gross margin 58.2% (p35) and PG FY2023 47.9% of net sales (p31). The verdict 'not strictly apples-to-apples' is right, but the reasons it gives are materially wrong, and they are the substance of the second half of the question. The GPI charge moved Colgate's gross profit by only $1M ($11,326 GAAP vs $11,327 ex-charges), and P&G's premium-product mix effects are an operating driver, not a basis difference; Colgate's margin also reflects mix. It misses the real basis difference: Colgate books shipping and handling in SG&A while P&G puts it in cost of products sold. Including those costs would cut Colgate's 2023 margin by 910 bps to about 49.1% vs P&G's 47.9%, so the gap shrinks from about 10.3 to about 1.2 points. It also misses the different fiscal periods (P&G Jul 2022-Jun 2023 vs CL calendar 2023). The user would come away thinking the ~10-point gap is mostly real, apart from a one-off charge and mix.
